opps.title: 5 accounts stopped ordering — $853 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, Blush Gentleman's Club, was worth 513 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: 8 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 664 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 664 cases and about $664 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.

opps.title: Midland Brewhouse (A) — down 36%, your #21 account
opps.body: Still ordering, but 564 cases lighter than last year (36%). It is your #21 account and 1.5% of your commission, so the slide is worth about $564 in modeled commission. The drop is concentrated in Corona Extra (-223 cases), Red Bull (-99 cases) — a mix problem you can work on the next visit, not a lost account.

opps.title: Heineken USA — 5% of your commission, down 13% YoY
opps.body: Sales are down 509 cases (13%) vs last year, but Heineken USA is still 5.0% of your total commission — your #6 brand. That decline has already cost about $509 in modeled commission, and recovering half of it is worth roughly $254. 115 accounts bought it last year; 113 have this year — 2 accounts stopped carrying it.
